battle.title: Java Fundamentals Showdown
battle.description: Variables, types, operators and control flow, tested the fun way.

questions.text: Which declaration creates a variable that can hold the whole number 42?
questions.explanation: int is Java's whole-number type. Java has no 'number' type, 'string' must be capitalised as String, and ':=' is not Java syntax.
Both operands are int, so / is integer division and drops the fraction (7 / 2 = 3). The % operator gives the remainder, 1.

questions.text: You need to repeat a block of code exactly 10 times and you know the number up front. Which construct fits best?
options: A for loop with a counter
A while(true) loop with no exit
questions.answer: A for loop with a counter
questions.explanation: A for loop packs the start, the stop condition and the step in one line, which is ideal when the repeat count is known. Copy-pasting is error-prone and while(true) never ends on its own.
continue skips the rest of the loop body for even i, so only 1 and 3 are added: 1 + 3 = 4.

questions.text: What is the value of x after:  int x = 5; x += 3; x *= 2;
questions.explanation: x += 3 makes x 8, then x *= 2 makes it 16. The compound operators apply one after the other, each using the current value.

coding.title: Sum of Even Numbers
coding.description: Read n and then n integers. Print the sum of the integers that are even (zero counts as even). If there are none, print 0.
coding.inputDescription: Line 1: n. Line 2: n integers separated by spaces.
coding.outputDescription: A single integer: the sum of the even numbers.

debug.title: The Off-By-One Total
debug.description: The program reads n and then n integers and should print their sum. It prints the wrong total. Input: n, then n integers on the next line. Output: the sum.
hints: Try it with a single number, for example n = 1. What should it print, and what does it print?
The total ignores something. Look at where the summing loop starts.
Arrays in Java start at index 0. A loop starting at 1 skips the first element: a classic off-by-one.
Start the summing loop at i = 0 so every element is added.
